newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Talks to avert Colombian strike break down, no deal.
newsitem.headline: Talks to avert Colombian strike break down, no deal.

text.p: Talks between the Colombian government and union representatives aimed at averting a nationwide state workers' strike broke down early on Sunday without agreement, the head of the main oil workers' union said.
Failure to reach a deal means that the strike, scheduled to begin on February 11, is almost certain to go ahead, he said.
The state workers are protesting against below-inflation wage rises, after being granted a 13.5 percent weighted increase, well under the 1996 inflation level of 21.63 percent.

They are also taking action against what they see as the erosion of labour rights by the government and plans for what they fear will spell the creeping privatisation of telecommunications, the oil industry and parts of the water distribution services.

Unions and government ministers were locked in talks most of Saturday but by the early hours of Sunday the two sides were still as far apart as ever, Hernando Hernandez, leader of the hardline oil workers' union, told Reuters.

"The government merely ratified its position on salaries and on privatisation. It offered a public forum on the privatisation issue but we are not calling a strike simply to win the promise of future discussions," Hernandez said.
"We have taken down the government's position in writing and will meet Sunday morning but as the position is now, the strike is definitely on," he added.
